cards.front: What is the primary function of the cardiovascular system?
cards.back: To transport oxygen, nutrients, and waste products throughout the body via blood circulation

cards.front: What is the normal resting heart rate for adults?
cards.back: 60-100 beats per minute - varies based on age, fitness level, and health conditions

cards.front: What is the main function of the respiratory system?
cards.back: To exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide between the body and the environment

cards.front: What is the normal blood pressure range for adults?
cards.back: Less than 120/80 mmHg - systolic pressure over diastolic pressure

cards.front: What is the primary function of the nervous system?
cards.back: To coordinate and control body functions through electrical and chemical signals

cards.front: What is the difference between arteries and veins?
cards.back: Arteries carry blood away from the heart, while veins carry blood toward the heart

cards.front: What is the main function of the digestive system?
cards.back: To break down food, absorb nutrients, and eliminate waste products

cards.front: What is the normal body temperature range?
cards.back: 97.8°F to 99.1°F (36.5°C to 37.3°C) - varies slightly among individuals

cards.front: What is the primary function of the immune system?
cards.back: To protect the body from harmful substances, pathogens, and abnormal cells

cards.front: What is the difference between aerobic and anaerobic exercise?
cards.back: Aerobic uses oxygen for energy (endurance), while anaerobic doesn't use oxygen (short bursts)

cards.front: What is the main function of the endocrine system?
cards.back: To regulate body functions through hormone production and secretion

cards.front: What is the normal range for blood glucose levels?
cards.back: 70-100 mg/dL when fasting, less than 140 mg/dL two hours after eating

cards.front: What is the primary function of the musculoskeletal system?
cards.back: To provide structure, support, and movement for the body

cards.front: What is the difference between acute and chronic diseases?
cards.back: Acute diseases develop quickly and are short-term, while chronic diseases develop slowly and are long-term

cards.front: What is the main function of the urinary system?
cards.back: To filter blood, remove waste products, and maintain fluid and electrolyte balance

cards.front: What is the normal range for cholesterol levels?
cards.back: Total cholesterol less than 200 mg/dL, LDL less than 100 mg/dL, HDL above 40 mg/dL

cards.front: What is the primary function of the integumentary system?
cards.back: To protect the body from external damage and regulate temperature

cards.front: What is the difference between pathogens and antigens?
cards.back: Pathogens cause disease, while antigens are substances that trigger immune responses

cards.front: What is the main function of the lymphatic system?
cards.back: To transport lymph, fight infections, and maintain fluid balance

cards.front: What is the normal range for hemoglobin levels?
cards.back: 12-16 g/dL for women, 14-18 g/dL for men - varies with age and health

cards.front: What is the primary function of the reproductive system?
cards.back: To produce offspring and maintain sexual characteristics

cards.front: What is the difference between vitamins and minerals?
cards.back: Vitamins are organic compounds needed in small amounts, while minerals are inorganic elements

cards.front: What is the main function of the skeletal system?
cards.back: To provide structure, protect organs, and store minerals like calcium

cards.front: What is the normal range for white blood cell count?
cards.back: 4,500-11,000 cells per microliter of blood - varies with age and health

cards.front: What is the primary function of the muscular system?
cards.back: To provide movement, maintain posture, and generate heat

cards.front: What is the difference between infectious and non-infectious diseases?
cards.back: Infectious diseases are caused by pathogens and can spread, while non-infectious diseases are not contagious

cards.front: What is the main function of the liver?
cards.back: To filter blood, produce bile, store nutrients, and detoxify harmful substances

cards.front: What is the normal range for platelet count?
cards.back: 150,000-450,000 platelets per microliter of blood

cards.front: What is the primary function of the kidneys?
cards.back: To filter blood, remove waste products, and maintain fluid and electrolyte balance

cards.front: What is the difference between prevention and treatment?
cards.back: Prevention stops disease before it occurs, while treatment manages existing disease

cards.front: What is the main function of the pancreas?
cards.back: To produce digestive enzymes and hormones like insulin and glucagon

cards.front: What is the normal range for blood pH?
cards.back: 7.35-7.45 - slightly alkaline, critical for proper body function

cards.front: What is the primary function of the brain?
cards.back: To control body functions, process information, and coordinate responses

cards.front: What is the difference between symptoms and signs?
cards.back: Symptoms are what patients feel, while signs are what healthcare providers observe

cards.front: What is the main function of the lungs?
cards.back: To exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide between blood and air

cards.front: What is the normal range for oxygen saturation?
cards.back: 95-100% - percentage of hemoglobin carrying oxygen

cards.front: What is the primary function of the heart?
cards.back: To pump blood throughout the body and maintain circulation

cards.front: What is the difference between diagnosis and prognosis?
cards.back: Diagnosis identifies the disease, while prognosis predicts the likely outcome

cards.front: What is the main function of the stomach?
cards.back: To break down food mechanically and chemically, and begin protein digestion

cards.front: What is the normal range for respiratory rate?
cards.back: 12-20 breaths per minute for adults - varies with age and activity

cards.front: What is the primary function of the small intestine?
cards.back: To absorb nutrients from digested food into the bloodstream

cards.front: What is the difference between immunity and resistance?
cards.back: Immunity is protection against specific diseases, while resistance is general ability to fight disease

cards.front: What is the main function of the large intestine?
cards.back: To absorb water and electrolytes, and form and store feces

cards.front: What is the normal range for body mass index (BMI)?
cards.back: 18.5-24.9 kg/m² for adults - indicates healthy weight range

cards.front: What is the primary function of the thyroid gland?
cards.back: To produce hormones that regulate metabolism and growth

cards.front: What is the difference between acute and chronic pain?
cards.back: Acute pain is short-term and protective, while chronic pain persists beyond normal healing time

cards.front: What is the main function of the adrenal glands?
cards.back: To produce hormones that regulate stress response and metabolism

cards.front: What is the normal range for blood pressure in children?
cards.back: Varies by age, height, and gender - generally lower than adults

cards.front: What is the primary function of the pituitary gland?
cards.back: To produce hormones that control other endocrine glands and body functions

cards.front: What is the difference between communicable and non-communicable diseases?
cards.back: Communicable diseases can spread between people, while non-communicable diseases cannot

cards.front: What is the main function of the gallbladder?
cards.back: To store and concentrate bile produced by the liver

cards.front: What is the normal range for red blood cell count?
cards.back: 4.2-5.4 million cells per microliter for women, 4.7-6.1 million for men

cards.front: What is the primary function of the spleen?
cards.back: To filter blood, remove old red blood cells, and store platelets
